Data sanitization is the process of removing or modifying sensitive information from data before it is stored, transmitted, or used in any way. The goal of data sanitization is to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive information and protect against potential security breaches.
When data is accepted as input from users, there is no guarantee that all malicious code will not be included with the data. This means that even if the data is sanitized at some point after being accepted as input, there may still be vulnerabilities present in the system that could allow attackers to exploit these vulnerabilities to gain access to sensitive information.
On the other hand, when data is only used for processing and output, there is less risk of introducing malicious code into the system. By sanitizing the data only when it is needed for use, rather than during the entire lifecycle of its acceptance and storage, organizations can reduce their exposure to potential security threats.
In summary, data sanitization should be performed on output/processing instead of when accepting user input because it reduces the risk of introducing malicious code into the system and protects against potential security breaches.
